published_pulse.commissioned_thesis: Across contemporary technical discourse, confidence is increasingly revealed as an optical artifact of how we measure. When automated evaluations fracture under real-world complexity, we discover that intelligent systems can be steered into performing caution or conviction on command, yet remain structurally blind to their own missteps in real time. The climate today is defined by this widening parallax: an outward choreography of calibrated poise that masks an inability to self-monitor from within.
